📌 Prediction Markets: Trading on Future Events

Main Points
⏺ Prediction markets let you trade on the outcome of events like elections, sports, or crypto decisions
⏺ Prices act like probabilities, showing what the crowd “thinks” will happen
⏺ This post explains how prediction markets turn opinions into tradable assets

1️⃣ Core Idea — instead of just guessing who will win, you buy “Yes” or “No” shares tied to a specific outcome
2️⃣ Pricing — if a “Yes” share trades at $0.70, the market is roughly saying there’s a 70% chance of that result
3️⃣ Settlement — after the event, winning shares pay out $1 while losing ones go to zero
4️⃣ Use Cases — forecasting politics, economic data, protocol decisions, and even on-chain governance outcomes
5️⃣ Signal Power — because people risk real money, prediction markets can sometimes be more accurate than polls or surveys

Final Thoughts

Prediction markets turn beliefs into positions — the stronger your conviction, the more you’re willing to back it with real capital.

📌 How will ESMA supervise crypto firms under MiCA in 2027? 

📣 The European Securities and Markets Authority has set operational resilience, outsourcing and sufficient EU based operations among its main crypto supervisory priorities for 2027 as the bloc moves further into enforcement of the Markets in Crypto Assets Regulation. 

🌐 ESMA said in its 2027 work program published Monday that its work on MiCA will concentrate on coordinating national regulators and developing more consistent supervision of crypto asset service providers across the European Union. The program comes as the regulator moves from writing and implementing MiCA rules toward overseeing how licensed firms comply with them in practice.  Chair Verena Ross described the change during a meeting of the European Parliament’s Committee on Economic and Monetary Affairs, saying ESMA’s MiCA work had moved “from rulemaking towards supervision and convergence.” 

⭐️ Operational resilience will be one of the main areas under scrutiny as ESMA works with national competent authorities responsible for supervising CASPs. Outsourcing risks, liquidity, reverse solicitation and the classification of crypto assets are among the other areas identified for coordinated work in 2027. Supervisors will pay attention to whether firms maintain sufficient operations within the EU instead of relying heavily on functions or infrastructure based elsewhere.

The Trump administration imposed today (Friday) extensive economic sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague, just hours after former judge Navanethem Pillay of the court was announced as the recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in an official statement, called the tribunal a "rogue court" and made it clear that the United States will prohibit any dealings or provision of commercial services to the institution itself, with the aim of cutting off its resources and silencing its activities: "President Trump will never allow the court to prosecute Americans. Either the court ceases its threats, or we will put an end to it." This unusual measure, intended to prevent global companies from providing banking, insurance, and software services to the court, comes in the wake of Washington's anger over arrest warrants issued against senior Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as well as past investigations into American soldiers. This move puts the United States on a direct diplomatic collision course with its allies in Europe, most of whom are members of the Rome Statute and fund the court.

🔖 Japanese police have arrested two people suspected of helping a fake police fraud group steal cryptocurrency worth approximately 81 million yen from a woman in her 40s. ⚠️ FNN reported that the caller told the woman her card appeared among accounts connected with the supposed money laundering investigation.
